properties.trigger: any competition in baseball: a professional league and its affiliates, college, youth, adult recreational hardball, or a fantasy baseball league; positions, stat keys, stages, run rules, suspended games, rosters, transactions, umpires
properties.scope: competition, season, team, person, event, stat_line

data.short_description: Baseball at every level, from tee-ball to a 30-team national professional league and fantasy leagues built on it: nine innings and extra innings, the automatic runner, doubleheaders and seven-inning games, suspended and called games, run rules, positions including two-way players, batting, pitching (outs, not fractional innings) and fielding keys with the derived rates, standings with games back and the official tiebreakers, roster lists and transactions as designations only, umpire roles, and the fantasy slots, categories and default scoring.

lore.title: Overview
lore.content:
Sport: baseball, at every level: a 30-team national professional league and its affiliated minor leagues, the top leagues of Japan, Korea, Taiwan, Mexico and the Caribbean, college and school ball, youth leagues from tee-ball to under-18, independent and summer collegiate leagues, adult recreational hardball, and fantasy baseball built on any of them. Code baseball. Slow-pitch and fast-pitch softball are a separate pack (code softball). Shared keys are spelled identically in the baseball and softball packs: decided_by run_rule, called_game and time_limit; stat keys outs_pitched and games_booked; and the exhibition tag on match lines that must not sum into a season.
A match is a game. Nine innings by default; each inning has a top (away team bats) and a bottom (home team bats), three outs per half-inning. The home team does not bat in the bottom of the ninth (or of any later inning) if it already leads, written X in a linescore. A game tied after nine goes to extra innings, one full inning at a time, until one side leads after a completed inning or the home team goes ahead in the bottom half. Many leagues now start every extra inning with an automatic runner on second base; the pack calls this the automatic-runner rule and the run that runner scores is unearned (it does not count against the pitcher's earned_runs). A game scheduled for fewer than nine innings (seven-inning doubleheader games, most youth and some college games) records its scheduled length in event.regulation_length as "7" and carries the tag seven-inning. Innings in score_display are written as a count: "7-6 (12)" for twelve innings, "8-6 (6.5, rain)" for a game called in the bottom of the seventh.
The single score number is runs: home_score and away_score are the final runs. A regulation nine-inning game needs nothing in score_display; use it for extra innings, called games, run-rule games, suspended games (both dates) and forfeits ("9-0 (forfeit)"). A linescore, when the owner keeps one, lives in event.periods: one object per inning with number, home and away (away is the top half, home the bottom; home null for an inning the home team did not bat, the X in a printed linescore); periods is optional and the runs on the event are the headline it sums to.
Results: home_win or away_win. Professional baseball has no ties; a game that cannot be finished is suspended and resumed or replayed. Ties exist in the top Japanese league (after twelve innings in the regular season), in some youth and recreational leagues with a time limit or inning cap, and in spring exhibitions, where result is tie and decided_by time_limit or inning_limit. Never draw. no_result for a game that was abandoned and will be neither resumed nor replayed.
decided_by: regulation, extra_innings, run_rule, called_game, time_limit, inning_limit, forfeit, tiebreaker_game. Use run_rule for every mercy rule at every level, so a mixed world with softball reads one way.
Default competition: level pro, format league_playoffs, scoring_system win_loss, rounds_total blank (baseball has no rounds; the schedule is a date range). A regular season at the top level is 162 games per team over about 186 days with an all-star break in the middle; college plays about 56; youth seasons run 12 to 20 games; a rec league 14 to 30. Season label is the single year the season is played ("2026"); a winter league that straddles the new year uses "2026-27". Season tag <competition-fragment>-<label>, e.g. riverside-hardball-2026. Every entity in this sport carries the tag baseball.
Home and away: the home team bats second and is listed second in a line like "Rovers at Riverside". A neutral-site game (a tournament, an international series, a youth regional) uses neutral_site true with neutral_first for the team listed first, who bats first. Doubleheaders are two separate match events on the same date with round "Game 1" and "Game 2"; a split doubleheader (two gates) is the same with date_hour on each.
Stats live on stat_lines in this pack's vocabulary. A player who both pitches and hits in the same game (a two-way player, or a pitcher batting in a league without the designated hitter) has one match stat_line holding both groups; the key names never collide because batting keys are plain (strikeouts, hits, walks) and pitching keys end in _pitching or _allowed.
The designated hitter (DH) is now universal at the top professional level and in most leagues below it; a few college conferences and many rec leagues let pitchers hit. Whether a competition uses the DH is a House rules fact on the competition.

lore.title: Positions
lore.content:
Position codes on PLAYS_FOR.position and secondary_positions, and on PLAYED_IN.position for the position played on the day. One primary per player; list the rest in secondary_positions.
P: pitcher, when the owner does not split starters and relievers
SP: starting pitcher
RP: relief pitcher
CL: closer (a relief pitcher who finishes close games; role on the staff, used as a position code because fantasy and depth charts treat it as one)
C: catcher
1B: first base
2B: second base
3B: third base
SS: shortstop
LF: left field
CF: center field
RF: right field
DH: designated hitter (bats, does not field)
IF: infielder, when the owner does not pin a player to one infield spot
OF: outfielder, when the owner does not pin a player to one outfield spot
UT: utility, plays infield and outfield
TWP: two-way player, a pitcher who also bats regularly (list SP or RP and the hitting position in secondary_positions)
On-the-day only, on PLAYED_IN.position, never on a roster edge:
PH: pinch hitter
PR: pinch runner
DEF: defensive substitute with no plate appearance
Scorer's position numbers (1 pitcher, 2 catcher, 3 first base, 4 second base, 5 third base, 6 shortstop, 7 left field, 8 center field, 9 right field) are used in lore when transcribing a scorebook ("6-4-3 double play") but never as position codes.
Depth: starting pitchers are role rotation on PLAYS_FOR with depth_order 1 for the ace and 5 for the fifth starter, and for position players 1 is the everyday starter at that position. The bullpen is role bench with position RP or CL; position players who start most days are role starter.
Handedness on person.handedness: bats_right_throws_right, bats_left_throws_left, bats_left_throws_right, bats_right_throws_left, bats_both_throws_right, bats_both_throws_left. "Switch hitter" means bats_both. Record it only when the owner gives it.

lore.title: Stages and rounds
lore.content:
stage values on event and season:
spring_training: pre-season exhibition games at the top level
preseason: pre-season games below the top level (college scrimmages, youth practice games)
exhibition: a one-off game that counts for nothing, including the all-star game (tag all-star) and charity games
regular_season: the league schedule
tiebreaker: a one-game playoff to settle a tie for a division or wild-card place when the league plays them off rather than using tiebreakers (decided_by tiebreaker_game on the game itself)
wildcard: the first postseason round (best-of-three at the top level)
divisional: the division series (best-of-five)
league_championship: the league/pennant series (best-of-seven)
final: the championship series (best-of-seven); at the top level the final is the only round where the two leagues meet, so neutral_site is false and home field goes to the better regular-season record
playoff: any postseason game in a league with a simpler bracket (youth, rec, college conference tournaments) when the round names above do not fit
regional, super_regional, national_championship: the college postseason tiers
district, sectional, state, regional_tournament, international_final: the youth tournament ladder, when the owner tracks it
consolation: a losers'-bracket game in a double-elimination tournament
Series: a best-of-N round is a parent event (event_type match, stage from the list above, score_display "4-2", result from the first-named team's point of view, date_* of game one and end_date of the clincher) with one child event per game, round "Game N", PART_OF the parent. The parent carries no runs in home_score/away_score; leave them null and put the series count in score_display. A regular-season series (three or four games against the same opponent) is not a parent event; it is just consecutive games.
round on a match event: "Game 1"/"Game 2" for a doubleheader; "Game N" inside a series; "Replay" for a replay from scratch of an abandoned game (a postponed game keeps its round and moves its date); "Opening Day" is a tag, not a round. Baseball has no weeks or matchdays, so season.current_round is left blank and season.stage carries the phase; a fantasy season does use round "Week N".
decided_by values: regulation (nine, or the scheduled length), extra_innings, run_rule (any mercy rule at any level), called_game (shortened by weather or light and official), time_limit (youth and rec curfews), inning_limit (a league cap on extra innings, e.g. twelve in the top Japanese league), forfeit, tiebreaker_game (on the one-game playoff itself), walkover (an opponent did not show and no score is awarded by rule).
Season stages in order for a pro season: spring_training, regular_season, postseason (season.stage value while the bracket runs; the events carry wildcard/divisional/league_championship/final), offseason. For college: preseason, regular_season, conference_tournament, regional, super_regional, national_championship, offseason. For youth and rec: preseason, regular_season, playoff, offseason.

lore.title: Stat keys
lore.content:
All keys lowercase snake_case, values numbers, null for not recorded. Store counting stats; rate stats are derived unless marked stored. A derived number is computed only over lines where every component it needs is non-null, and the answer says how many games that covers (books are partial below the pro level). Match lines may be tagged exhibition to keep them out of season totals. Every stat_line carries completeness: full when every key this chunk lists for its scope was recorded, partial when any key is null because nobody kept it, unknown for typed-in totals of unknown coverage; sums skip nulls and a season line built from any partial line is partial.
PLAYER BATTING (match, season, career, split lines)
games_batting: games with a plate appearance or a defensive appearance (stored on season/career lines; equals games_played when not split)
plate_appearances: trips to the plate with a result (stored; if unknown derive as at_bats + walks + hit_by_pitch + sacrifice_flies + sacrifice_bunts + catcher_interference over non-null components)
at_bats: official at bats (stored)
runs: runs scored (stored)
hits: all hits (stored)
singles: derived, hits - doubles - triples - home_runs (store only if counted directly)
doubles: two-base hits (stored)
triples: three-base hits (stored)
home_runs: home runs (stored)
rbi: runs batted in (stored)
walks: bases on balls including intentional (stored)
intentional_walks: intentional walks (stored)
hit_by_pitch: hit by pitch (stored)
strikeouts: struck out as a batter (stored)
sacrifice_flies: sac flies (stored)
sacrifice_bunts: sac bunts (stored)
stolen_bases: stolen bases (stored)
caught_stealing: caught stealing (stored)
grounded_into_double_play: GIDP (stored)
catcher_interference: times awarded first on catcher's interference (stored, rare)
reached_on_error: reached on an error (stored; an at bat, not a hit)
left_on_base_batting: runners left on base by this batter (stored when the book has it)
pitches_seen: pitches faced (stored when tracked)
total_bases: derived, singles + 2*doubles + 3*triples + 4*home_runs
extra_base_hits: derived, doubles + triples + home_runs
batting_average: derived, hits / at_bats, written .312; qualifying minimum 3.1 plate appearances per team game at the pro level, House rules below it
on_base_percentage: derived, (hits + walks + hit_by_pitch) / (at_bats + walks + hit_by_pitch + sacrifice_flies)
slugging_percentage: derived, total_bases / at_bats
ops: derived, on_base_percentage + slugging_percentage
isolated_power: derived, slugging_percentage - batting_average
babip: derived, (hits - home_runs) / (at_bats - strikeouts - home_runs + sacrifice_flies)
strikeout_rate: derived, strikeouts / plate_appearances
walk_rate: derived, walks / plate_appearances
stolen_base_percentage: derived, stolen_bases / (stolen_bases + caught_stealing)
Published advanced numbers the owner imports (wrc_plus, ops_plus, war, woba) are stored rate stats with source import and the site named in source_url; the AI never computes them.
PLAYER PITCHING (same lines; a two-way player's line holds both groups)
games_pitched: appearances (stored)
games_started_pitching: starts (stored)
games_finished: games in which this pitcher recorded the last out (stored)
complete_games: complete games (stored; a complete game is the whole scheduled length, seven in a seven-inning game)
shutouts: complete games with no runs allowed (stored)
outs_pitched: outs recorded while pitching (stored; the honest unit because thirds of an inning do not add)
innings_pitched: derived, outs_pitched / 3, written 41.2 for 125 outs (the digit after the point is thirds, never a decimal)
batters_faced: batters faced (stored)
hits_allowed: hits allowed (stored)
runs_allowed: runs allowed, earned and unearned (stored)
earned_runs: earned runs (stored; the automatic runner's run is unearned)
walks_allowed: walks issued including intentional (stored)
intentional_walks_allowed: intentional walks issued (stored)
strikeouts_pitching: batters struck out (stored)
home_runs_allowed: home runs allowed (stored)
hit_batters: batters hit by pitch (stored)
wild_pitches: wild pitches (stored)
balks: balks (stored)
pitches: pitches thrown (stored; also the youth pitch-count stat)
strikes: strikes thrown, including fouls and balls in play (stored)
ground_outs_pitching, fly_outs_pitching: batted-ball outs by type (stored when tracked)
pickoffs: runners picked off (stored)
stolen_bases_allowed, caught_stealing_pitching: running game against this pitcher (stored)
wins_pitching: wins credited (stored; the official scorer decides, never derive)
losses_pitching: losses credited (stored)
saves: saves (stored)
save_opportunities: save chances (stored)
blown_saves: blown saves (stored)
holds: holds (stored)
quality_starts: starts of at least 18 outs with 3 or fewer earned runs (stored as a count; the AI may derive it per match when outs_pitched and earned_runs are present)
era: derived, earned_runs * 9 / (outs_pitched / 3), written 3.27; use 9 even in seven-inning leagues unless House rules say 7
whip: derived, (walks_allowed + hits_allowed) / (outs_pitched / 3)
k_per_9: derived, strikeouts_pitching * 27 / outs_pitched
bb_per_9: derived, walks_allowed * 27 / outs_pitched
hr_per_9: derived, home_runs_allowed * 27 / outs_pitched
k_bb_ratio: derived, strikeouts_pitching / walks_allowed
strike_percentage: derived, strikes / pitches
opponent_batting_average: derived, hits_allowed / (batters_faced - walks_allowed - hit_batters - sacrifice_flies_allowed - sacrifice_bunts_allowed - catcher_interference_allowed) when those are tracked, otherwise say it is not computable
fip: stored only when imported (needs a league constant the world does not hold)
PLAYER FIELDING (per position when the owner splits them: use a split line with split_label the position, otherwise one group on the main line)
games_fielding: games at the position (stored)
innings_fielded_outs: defensive outs on the field at the position (stored; divide by 3 for innings)
putouts: putouts (stored)
assists: assists (stored)
errors: errors (stored)
double_plays: double plays taken part in (stored)
triple_plays: triple plays (stored)
total_chances: derived, putouts + assists + errors
fielding_percentage: derived, (putouts + assists) / total_chances, written .987
passed_balls: catchers (stored)
stolen_bases_allowed_catching, caught_stealing_catching: catchers' running game (stored)
caught_stealing_percentage: derived, caught_stealing_catching / (stolen_bases_allowed_catching + caught_stealing_catching)
pickoffs_catching: catcher pickoffs (stored)
outfield_assists: outfielders (stored)
TEAM (match lines carry the box; season lines carry totals and the standings keys in the Standings chunk; runs stay on the event and are never repeated on a team line)
Runs by inning are not stat keys: the linescore lives in event.periods (number, home, away per inning, optional), and runs stay on the event.
hits, errors, left_on_base: the box-score line beneath the linescore (stored)
doubles, triples, home_runs, walks, strikeouts, stolen_bases, caught_stealing, hit_by_pitch, sacrifice_flies, sacrifice_bunts, grounded_into_double_play: team batting totals (stored, same spelling as the player keys)
double_plays_turned: defensive double plays (stored)
pitchers_used: pitchers used in the game (stored)
pitches_thrown_team: team pitch count (stored)
runners_in_scoring_position_hits, runners_in_scoring_position_at_bats: the RISP line (stored)
attendance stays on the event; time_of_game_seconds is a team match key (stored, the game's length in seconds, as the base requires for durations)
Season-only team keys beyond standings: games_booked (completed games that have any match stat_line at all, so averages can be quoted honestly), runs_per_game (derived, runs_for / games_played), team_era, team_batting_average, team_ops (derived from the summed components)
FANTASY (player lines RECORDED_IN the fantasy matchup or the fantasy season)
fantasy_points: points scored under the league's table (stored)
projected_points: the platform's projection (stored)
The real stats used to compute points are the batting and pitching keys above, repeated on the fantasy line with source import when the manager wants them.
WORKLOAD AND ELIGIBILITY (counts the league itself keeps; never a health fact)
pitches is the youth pitch-count stat; days_rest_required is derived from the House rules table, not stored
options_used: minor-league option assignments used this season (team/player season line, stored)
games_at_position_<pos> is not a key; use a split line per position for fantasy eligibility counts

lore.title: Standings
lore.content:
Team season line keys (RECORDED_IN the season, STAT_OF the team): wins, losses, ties (only in leagues that have them), runs_for, runs_against, home_wins, home_losses, away_wins, away_losses, division_wins, division_losses, league_wins, league_losses, interleague_wins, interleague_losses, one_run_wins, one_run_losses, extra_innings_wins, extra_innings_losses, last_10_wins, last_10_losses, streak (positive for a winning streak, negative for losing), forfeit_wins, forfeit_losses, games_booked. Head-to-head records against each opponent are not keys; the AI reads them from COMPETED_IN edges when a tiebreaker needs them.
Derived: games_played = wins + losses + ties; win_pct = (wins + 0.5 * ties) / games_played written .593; run_differential = runs_for - runs_against; games_back = ((leader_wins - team_wins) + (team_losses - leader_losses)) / 2, written 3.5 and "-" for the leader; wildcard_games_back the same against the last team currently holding a wild-card place, written "+2.0" for teams inside the line; elimination_number = games_remaining_for_team + leader_wins - team_wins + 1 (say E when it reaches 0); pythagorean_wins = games_played * runs_for^1.83 / (runs_for^1.83 + runs_against^1.83) when asked.
Columns to show: W, L, PCT, GB, (WCGB when a wild card exists), RS, RA, DIFF, HOME, AWAY, L10, STRK. Division tables first, then the wild-card table for each league. Ties as a T column only in leagues that have them. On COMPETES_IN, conference is the league ("League A") and group is the division alone ("East"); the league and division are also tags on the team.
A division or wild-card table is only honest when every team's games are on file. A fan logging one team gets that team's record, splits, run differential and streak, and the words "the rest of the division is not on file"; offer a web lookup for a public league. Never fill in another team's record from memory.
Tiebreakers at the top professional level, in order, applied to teams tied for a division title or a postseason place (there are no tiebreaker games; everything is decided on these):
1. Head-to-head record among the tied teams.
2. Intradivision record (division_wins / division_losses).
3. Interdivision record within the league (league record minus division record).
4. Record in the last half of intraleague games, then the last half plus one game, and so on back, until the tie breaks.
Postseason seeding at the top level: three division winners seeded 1-3 by record, three wild cards seeded 4-6; the 1 and 2 seeds skip the wild-card round; no reseeding. Home field in a series goes to the higher seed; in the final, to the better regular-season record, broken by the same tiebreakers.
College and youth tiebreakers vary; a league's own order goes in a House rules chunk on the competition and overrides this list. Common defaults: head-to-head, then run differential in games between the tied teams, then runs allowed, then coin flip or draw (record the result and method in lore on the season).
Record forfeits as 9-0 in the score fields at every level unless House rules say otherwise, and count them in wins/losses and in forfeit_wins/forfeit_losses; never in runs_for/runs_against unless the league says so (the top level does not).

lore.title: Roster rules
lore.content:
Squad sizes by level (defaults; House rules override): top professional active roster 26 from opening day to 31 August and 28 from 1 September, with at most 13 pitchers (14 in September); a 40-man reserve list that the active roster sits inside; affiliated minor-league teams with their own active limits. College: 40 on the roster, 34 on a conference travel squad. Youth: 12 to 15. Rec: whatever shows up, usually 12 to 20 on the books.
Lists are roster designations, never reasons. PLAYS_FOR.roster_list takes these values: active (the 26/28-man or the game-day roster), forty_man (on the reserve list but not active; combine with role reserve), il_10 (pitchers and two-way players), il_15, il_60, dfa (designated for assignment: off the 40-man, in limbo for up to seven days), restricted, suspended_list, bereavement_or_paternity (never which; both are availability unavailable with no list name if the owner prefers), taxi (postseason or travel taxi squad), practice (college or youth practice-only player). Any injured list means availability unavailable, role injured_reserve, and nothing about why: not the body part, not the expected return, not the retroactive reason. If the owner types one, keep the list and the date and say in one line that this world keeps no health details.
Roles on PLAYS_FOR: starter (everyday position players), rotation (starting pitchers), bench (relievers and bench bats), reserve (on the 40-man but not active, or a youth/rec player who rarely plays), captain (where a league names one), practice_squad is not used in baseball, taxi only in the postseason.
Options and assignments: a player optioned or assigned to an affiliate that is PART_OF the parent team follows the base loan pattern: open a PLAYS_FOR edge to the affiliate with arrangement loan and acquired_via option, keep the parent edge open with role reserve and roster_list forty_man. A recall ends the affiliate edge and restores the parent edge's role. Each option assignment is a roster_move event (rule/baseball_transactions); options_used on the player's season line counts them (three option years per player, five assignments per season is the modern cap; the AI flags the sixth, it does not refuse). An outright assignment (cleared waivers, off the 40-man) is the same pattern with acquired_via outright and the parent edge's roster_list cleared.
Two-way players: position TWP, with the pitching role (SP or RP) and the hitting position in secondary_positions. Eligibility for the two-way designation (20 innings pitched and 20 games with three plate appearances as a hitter or DH in the current or prior season) is checked from season lines when the owner asks; the designation itself is a lore note on the person titled "Two-way designation" with the date.
Lineup rules to check before logging a lineup: nine in the batting order (ten in a youth or rec league with an extra hitter; House rules), each with a position; exactly one of each fielding position; a DH only if the competition uses one; a pitcher who is also the DH in a two-way lineup keeps DH eligibility after leaving the mound (the two-way rule) and is logged with position TWP on PLAYED_IN. A substitute entering mid-game gets PLAYED_IN started false, entered_at "7th inning", position on the day (PH, PR, DEF or the field position). Re-entry is not allowed at the pro and college level; many youth leagues allow a starter to re-enter once, which is a House rules fact.
Pitching rules the AI should know, not enforce: a starter needs 15 outs for a win (12 in a seven-inning game by local rule), a reliever can earn a win with fewer; a save needs the pitcher to finish a game his team won without receiving the win, entering with a lead of three or fewer, or with the tying run on deck, or pitching the last three innings; a hold is a save situation handed off with the lead intact. These are the official scorer's decisions, so the owner's or the box score's word wins; the AI never derives decisions.
Youth pitch limits and rest days: the league's table (pitches per day by league age, and rest days per pitch band) lives in a House rules chunk on the competition. The AI stores pitches on the match line and, when asked or when logging the next game's lineup, says whether a pitcher is eligible by that table. It never records a reason a pitcher is sitting out beyond the table itself.
Jersey numbers 0-99 at the top level; a change updates jersey_number in place with a lore note.
Coaching staff on STAFF_OF: manager (the baseball term for the head coach; title "Manager"); assistant_coach with title "Bench Coach", "Pitching Coach", "Hitting Coach", "First Base Coach", "Third Base Coach", "Bullpen Coach"; coordinator for "Director of Player Development" style roles; general_manager; president (title "President of Baseball Operations"); owner. Youth: head_coach, assistant_coach, team_parent, and scorer as title on role other. College: head_coach, assistant_coach with title ("Pitching Coach", "Recruiting Coordinator").
Ringers and subs in rec ball: PLAYS_FOR with arrangement substitute, started and ended the match date, lore note; a pick-up player who keeps coming back gets the edge left open.

lore.title: Officials
lore.content:
OFFICIATED.role values:
plate_umpire: behind the plate; the umpire-in-chief in a two- or three-umpire crew
base_umpire: any base umpire in a two- or three-umpire crew when the owner does not say which base
first_base_umpire, second_base_umpire, third_base_umpire: four-umpire crews
left_field_umpire, right_field_umpire: six-umpire postseason crews
crew_chief: the senior umpire of a pro crew (also carries one of the position roles for the game: two edges)
replay_official: the review umpire at the replay centre
official_scorer: the scorer who decides hits, errors, earned runs and pitching decisions (pro and college); at youth and rec level the person keeping the book is a scorer and is only recorded if the owner wants them
pitch_timer_operator, video_coordinator: only when the owner tracks them
Officials in a pro league are public professionals; youth and rec umpires are private people and get name and role only, never a web lookup. Ejections are a sporting fact: a lore chunk on the event titled "Ejections" with who and the inning, no further characterisation.

lore.title: Extended keys
lore.content: No extended keys yet. Keys the owner adds go here, one per line, dated, with meaning and whether stored or derived.

lore.title: Recreational
lore.content:
What a local adult hardball or youth league changes:
Game length: seven innings is normal, six in younger youth divisions, often with a time limit ("no new inning after 1h50"). Set regulation_length "7" (or "6") and tag seven-inning; decided_by time_limit when the clock ended it.
Run rules: typical tables are 15 after 3, 10 after 4 or 5, 8 after 5 at youth level; 10 after 7 in adult leagues. The table is House rules; the game records decided_by run_rule and the innings in score_display.
Ties: allowed in many leagues when the time limit hits. result tie, both COMPETED_IN edges tie, counted as half a win in win_pct.
Rolling and free substitution: many youth leagues require every player to bat (continuous batting order) and play a minimum number of innings in the field. The lineup check uses the House rules count (e.g. "all present players bat; everyone plays six defensive outs"). PLAYED_IN lineup_order runs past nine. Re-entry of starters is usually allowed once.
Pitch counts: the league's pitch-count and rest table in House rules; pitches on the pitcher's match line; the AI answers eligibility from the table and the schedule (see Roster rules). Nothing about arms, ever.
Courtesy runners for the catcher or pitcher: PLAYED_IN with position PR and a lore note; no stat beyond runs for the runner.
Books are partial. Most weeks someone kept hits and runs and nobody kept walks. Store what was kept, leave the rest null, never write zero for "nobody counted", and quote every average with the number of games it covers. games_booked on the team season line says how many games have a book at all.
Co-ed and age rules: the pack stores no gender or age for anyone. Age division is a tag on the competition (u10, u12, u14, u18, over_35); eligibility is the owner's check. Youth players are is_minor true, first name plus last initial, position and team, nothing else, and are never looked up.
Ringers: arrangement substitute, one-day edge. League-wide pick-up players who float between teams get one edge per team.
Umpires: usually a two-umpire crew paid by the league, private people, name and role only.
Equipment rules (wood bat, bat drop, metal cleats) are House rules prose, not properties.
Dues and field fees are lore on the team in the owner's words, never per-person properties or payment details.
Weather: rainouts are postponed and rescheduled when the league has a makeup date; a game stopped with the required innings in (four and a half with the home team ahead or five, or the league's number) is completed with decided_by called_game; anything earlier is abandoned and replayed from scratch as a new event with round Replay, or resumed as a suspended game if the league does that (see Forfeits and abandonments).

lore.title: Professional
lore.content:
What the top level adds. The reference shape is a 30-team national professional league in two leagues of three five-team divisions, each team playing 162 games (balanced schedule: 13 against each division opponent, 6 or 7 against the other ten league opponents, 3 against every team in the other league). On COMPETES_IN, conference is the league ("League A") and group is the division ("East"); tags on the team are the league (league-a) and division (league-a-east). The top leagues of Japan and Korea are two leagues of six and one league of ten respectively; use the same pattern with the group label the league uses.
Postseason: twelve teams (six per league); stages wildcard (best of three, all games at the higher seed), divisional (best of five, 2-2-1), league_championship (best of seven, 2-3-2), final (best of seven, 2-3-2). Each round is a parent event with child games; the champion gets WON to the season with title Champion and the runner-up Runner-up. The final's most valuable player: WON from the person to the parent event with title "Series MVP".
Season awards as WON to the season: Most Valuable Player, Best Pitcher, Rookie of the Year, Manager of the Year, Reliever of the Year, Best Fielder (detail the position), Best Hitter by Position (detail the position), Batting Champion, Home Run Leader. Use these generic titles; the league's own award name may be quoted in detail if the owner uses it.
Draft: one event per draft, event_type draft, named "<Competition> Draft <year>", date of day one, end_date of the last day; twenty rounds at the top level plus competitive-balance and compensation picks after rounds 1 and 2 (detail "Round 1, Pick 14 (14 overall)", "CB-A, Pick 31", "Compensation, Pick 72"). Draftees go to an affiliate, not the parent club: PLAYS_FOR the affiliate (PART_OF the franchise) with acquired_via draft; undrafted signings are a signing event with detail "UDFA". International amateur signings are signing events with detail "international, <signing period>" and fee as text. The top Japanese and Korean leagues have their own drafts; the same pattern.
Transactions: see rule/baseball_transactions for the moves. Every move the owner records is an event (trade, signing, release, or roster_move) plus the edge changes it implies; the trade deadline (end of July at the top level) is a flag to ask, not a refusal. Waivers: a claimed player is a roster_move with detail "waiver claim from <team>" and the old edge ended; a player who clears is outrighted or released. The 40-man and the 26-man are roster_list values; the active roster count is checked when the owner asks ("you're at 27") and never enforced.
Contracts: fee as text on PLAYS_FOR ("6y/$150M", "1y/$740K pre-arb", "split contract") and in detail on the signing event; arbitration, extensions and opt-outs are signing events with detail starting "extension:" or "arbitration:"; service time is a lore chunk on the person titled "Service time" in the owner's words (years.days), never computed by the AI.
Modern stats: the owner may import published rate stats (war, wrc_plus, ops_plus, fip, xera, barrel_rate, exit_velocity_avg, sprint_speed, framing_runs, outs_above_average) as stored keys with source import and source_url; add them under Extended keys the first time, dated, marked stored. The AI never computes any of them.
Officials: four-umpire crews with a crew_chief, six in the postseason, replay_official at the review centre, an official_scorer per game. Pitch timer violations are lore on the event.
Ghost runner: the automatic runner starts every extra inning of the regular season; the postseason plays full extra innings without one. Tag the event automatic-runner when it mattered; the run is unearned.
Interleague and the universal DH: every game uses the DH; the final is played under the same rules in both parks. Ties do not exist; a game that cannot finish is suspended and resumed (Forfeits and abandonments).
All-star game: stage exhibition, tag all-star, neutral_site false (the host club is home), match lines tagged exhibition.
Spring training: stage spring_training; results and lines are kept if the owner wants them and never roll into the season.

lore.title: Fantasy
lore.content:
Baseball-specific material for rule/app_fantasy, which owns rosters, lineups, waivers, FAAB, trades, keepers, head-to-head matchups and category standings. This chunk supplies only the sport's vocabulary and defaults.
Slots (PLAYS_FOR.slot on the fantasy roster edge; PLAYED_IN.slot on the matchup): C, 1B, 2B, 3B, SS, OF, OF, OF, UTIL (any hitter), CI (corner infield 1B/3B) and MI (middle infield 2B/SS) in leagues that use them, DH (hitters only, some platforms), SP, SP, RP, RP, P, P (any pitcher), BN (bench), IL (injured-list slot: eligible only when the real player is on an injured list; the pack stores the slot and the real player's availability, nothing about why), NA (minor-league or not-active slot in dynasty leagues). Default roster: 13 hitters (C 1B 2B 3B SS OF OF OF UTIL + 4 BN shared), 9 pitchers (SP SP RP RP P P + BN), 23 to 26 total with 2 IL slots. Position eligibility: a hitter qualifies at a position with 20 games there the prior season or 10 this season on most platforms; the AI reads the real player's PLAYED_IN positions or split lines when asked and otherwise takes the owner's word.
Formats (competition.scoring_system): roto_5x5 (default), roto_custom, h2h_categories, h2h_points, points_season.
Rotisserie 5x5 categories (team season line, each category ranked across the league; the team's rotisserie points are the sum of its ranks with N points for first in an N-team league):
Hitting: runs, home_runs, rbi, stolen_bases, batting_average (derived from hits/at_bats on the team line).
Pitching: wins_pitching, saves, strikeouts_pitching, era (derived from earned_runs and outs_pitched), whip (derived from walks_allowed, hits_allowed, outs_pitched).
Common swaps for roto_custom and h2h_categories: on_base_percentage for batting_average, saves_plus_holds (stored as the sum) for saves, quality_starts for wins_pitching, ops, total_bases, strikeouts (hitter, negative), k_per_9, innings_pitched (as outs_pitched). A 6x6 adds ops and quality_starts. The league's list goes in a House rules chunk on the competition; the AI ranks only the keys listed there.
Category team lines: one season stat_line per fantasy team with the summed real stats of its active-slot players for the period (daily lineups: whatever the platform summed; the AI never re-sums daily). source import with the platform's URL. Head-to-head categories: the matchup event carries home_score/away_score as categories won, score_display "6-3-1".
Points-league default scoring (fantasy_points on the player's match or round line; override in House rules):
Hitting: single 1, double 2, triple 3, home_run 4, run 1, rbi 1, walk 1, hit_by_pitch 1, stolen_base 2, caught_stealing -1, strikeout -1 (optional), grounded_into_double_play -1 (optional).
Pitching: out_pitched 1 (so 3 per inning), strikeout_pitching 1, win 5, loss -5 (optional), save 5, hold 2 (optional), earned_run -2, hit_allowed -1, walk_allowed -1, hit_batter -1, quality_start 3 (optional), complete_game 3, shutout 3, no_hitter 5 (owner marks it).
Periods: baseball fantasy is daily (lineups lock at each game's first pitch) or weekly (lineups lock Monday). round on the matchup is "Week N" (scoring periods usually run Monday to Sunday; the first and last weeks and the all-star week are often long or short, so House rules state the calendar). Daily lineups are not stored by default; the matchup's totals are. If the owner dictates a day's lineup it goes in lore on the matchup titled "Lineup <date>".
Two-way players: platforms list the hitter and the pitcher as two roster entries; this world keeps one person with two slots when both are rostered (two PLAYS_FOR edges to the fantasy team, slot per side, lore note), and his fantasy_points line holds both groups.
Innings minimums (most roto leagues require a season total of outs_pitched from the team's pitchers, e.g. 900 innings = 2700 outs), games-played caps per position and start limits for pitchers are House rules the AI checks only when asked.
Draft defaults: snake, 23 rounds for a 23-man roster; auction with a $260 budget. Keepers and dynasty: keeper count and cost rules in House rules. The platform's player id goes in person.external_id.

lore.title: Glossary
lore.content: Automatic runner (ghost runner): the runner placed on second to start an extra inning; unearned if he scores. Battery: the pitcher and catcher. Bullpen: the relievers, and the place they warm up. Called game: a game shortened by weather or light that still counts because the required innings were played. Clinch: to secure a division or playoff place; a WON edge comes later, at season end. DFA: designated for assignment, removed from the 40-man with seven days to be traded, waived or released. Doubleheader: two games on one day; twin bill. Extra hitter (EH): a tenth batter in some youth and rec leagues who does not field. Games back (GB): how far behind the leader, half a game per unmatched win or loss. Hold: a reliever preserves a lead in a save situation without finishing. Linescore: runs by inning plus runs, hits and errors. Magic number: wins plus opponents' losses needed to clinch; computed on request from the team lines. No-hitter and perfect game: owner marks them; tag the event no-hitter or perfect-game and WON from the pitcher with title "No-hitter". Official game: five innings, or four and a half with the home team ahead (the league's number in House rules). Option: assigning a 40-man player to the minors without waivers; three option years per player. Outright: assigning a player to the minors after he clears waivers, removing him from the 40-man. Pennant: a league championship. Quality start: six innings, three or fewer earned runs. Run rule: the mercy rule, by any local name. Save: finishing a win in a save situation. Service time: days on the active roster or injured list; lore, never computed here. Suspended game: a game halted and completed later from the point of stoppage. Sweep: winning every game of a series. Tiebreaker game: a one-game playoff, used by some leagues instead of tiebreaker records. Twin bill: a doubleheader. Two-way player: a player who both pitches and hits regularly, position TWP. Utility (UT): plays several positions. Walk-off: a game ended by the home team's run in the bottom of the last inning; tag walk-off. Wild card: a postseason place for a non-division-winner, by record.

lore.title: Season calendar
lore.content:
Top-level professional season (northern hemisphere): spring training from mid-February (pitchers and catchers first) with exhibition games from late February; opening day in the last week of March; the all-star break in mid-July (the exhibition itself, plus a home run contest the pack does not score); the trade deadline at the end of July; rosters expand to 28 on 1 September; the regular season ends on the last Sunday of September or first of October; postseason through late October or early November; free agency opens five days after the final; the winter meetings and the unprotected-player draft in early December (a roster_move event per selection with detail "unprotected-player draft selection from <team>"); arbitration in January.
Winter leagues in the Caribbean and the southern hemisphere run October to February and use a two-year label ("2026-27").
The top Japanese league opens in late March and plays 143 games with a two-stage step-ladder postseason before its championship series in late October; the top Korean league plays 144 games from late March with a step-ladder postseason. Model each as its own competition with the pack's generic stage names (stage playoff for the step-ladder rounds, league_championship, final) and House rules for the tie rule (twelve innings, then a tie, in the regular season).
College: season from mid-February to late May, conference tournaments in late May, regionals and super regionals in early June, the national championship in mid-June; the amateur draft follows in July.
Youth: spring seasons from April to June, all-star tournaments through July and August on the district-sectional-state-regional-international ladder; fall ball September to November as a separate season with its own label ("Fall 2026").
Adult rec: spring and summer seasons, often a fall season; each is its own season of the same competition.
Fantasy: scoring periods start on opening day; most weekly leagues treat the opening partial week as Week 1 and the all-star week as a long week; the fantasy regular season ends with the real season or a week early so the playoffs finish before the last real week; House rules for the exact calendar.

lore.title: Forfeits and abandonments
lore.content:
Postponed (never started): status postponed, keep the entity, update date_* when the makeup date is set, note the original date in lore titled "Postponement". A makeup scheduled as part of a doubleheader gets round "Game 1" or "Game 2" and the other game's event is created alongside.
Suspended (started, will resume from the point of stoppage): status suspended. date_* stay the first day; end_date is the completion day; score_display during the gap reads "5-3, susp. top 6th, resumes 2026-07-19". On completion: status completed, end_date set, the final line in score_display ("7-5 (susp. 2026-07-02, completed 2026-07-19)"), and the result counts in the standings on the completion date. Match stat_lines stay on the one event and accumulate; the pitcher of record is whoever the official scorer says once it ends. A suspended game resumed at the other team's park keeps its home team (the home team still bats second) and gets a second HELD_AT edge with a lore note. At the top level a game is suspended rather than abandoned when it is stopped before becoming official, or stopped while tied after becoming official, or stopped in an inning in which the visiting team has taken the lead and the home team has not completed its half; in all other cases it is a called game and counts.
Called game (official, counts): status completed, decided_by called_game, the score when stopped, innings and reason in score_display.
Abandoned and replayed (started, will not resume): status abandoned, result no_result, the position when play stopped in score_display, the match lines kept but tagged exhibition (they do not count in that league, and the pack says so once; a league that counts the individual stats from a replayed game, as some youth leagues do, says so in House rules). The replay is a new event with round "Replay" and a lore note pointing at the abandoned one.
Run rule: status completed, decided_by run_rule, innings in score_display. The table is House rules per competition (the top professional level has none).
Forfeit: status forfeited, 9-0 in the score fields (7-0 in a seven-inning league if House rules say so), result for the non-offending side, decided_by forfeit, reason in lore in the league's words (not enough players, ejections leaving fewer than nine, refusal to continue). Forfeits count in wins/losses and forfeit_wins/forfeit_losses and not in runs_for/runs_against unless House rules say otherwise. Any innings actually played before the forfeit keep their match lines (the top level counts them; many rec leagues do not, so tag exhibition where House rules say so).
Walkover (opponent did not appear and the league awards no score): status forfeited with decided_by walkover, home_score and away_score null, result for the side that showed, lore note. Rare; most leagues simply forfeit.
No result (cancelled and never made up, e.g. the end-of-season rainout that does not affect the standings): status cancelled, result no_result, lore note "not made up".
Protests: a game played under protest is completed as scored, tagged under-protest, with the protest and its outcome in lore on the event titled "Protest"; if the league orders it replayed or resumed, follow the paragraphs above and note the ruling.
Tie at the end of the regular season for a postseason place: no tiebreaker game at the top level (tiebreaker records in the Standings chunk); leagues that do play one record it with stage tiebreaker and decided_by tiebreaker_game, and it counts as a regular-season game in every stat line.

properties.trigger: logging a baseball game: score, linescore, lineup, batting and pitching lines, a suspended or called game, a doubleheader, what to say about averages afterwards

data.short_description: The order of work for logging one baseball game at any level, from the score to the season lines, and how to quote the averages afterwards without overstating what the book holds.

lore.title: Logging a game
lore.content:
A baseball game at any level, logged in one pass. Read rule/recording_a_match and rule/stats first; this chunk is the order of work for this sport.
1. Find or create the game: search by the two teams and the date; a doubleheader is two events with round "Game 1"/"Game 2". A postponed game being made up is the existing event with a new date. A suspended game being completed is the existing event (Forfeits and abandonments in the pack).
2. Score: home_score and away_score as runs, status completed, decided_by (regulation unless something else), score_display only when needed (extra innings "(11)", called "(6.5, rain)", run rule "(4 inn.)", seven-inning "(7)", suspended with both dates, forfeit "9-0 (forfeit)"). result and the two COMPETED_IN results. Tag the event baseball, the season tag, match, and any of walk-off, no-hitter, perfect-game, automatic-runner, seven-inning, all-star, under-protest when they apply.
3. Linescore, if given: event.periods, one object per inning with number, home and away; the home team's unplayed bottom of the ninth is home null, not zero. The box-score line beneath it (hits, errors, left_on_base) goes on the team match stat_line. Runs are already on the event; do not repeat them as a key.
4. Lineups, only when the competition is tagged lineups-tracked: one PLAYED_IN per player with for_team, lineup_order 1-9 (or more with an extra hitter or continuous order), position on the day, started true; substitutes with started false, entered_at the inning, position PH/PR/DEF or the field spot. Check the lineup against Roster rules (nine with positions, one of each, DH only if the competition uses one) and say what is off; log anyway if the owner says so.
5. Batting lines: one match stat_line per batter the owner has numbers for, keys from Stat keys, nulls for anything not kept, completeness partial when any key is null and full when the whole line is complete. "2-for-4 with a double and 2 RBI" is at_bats 4, hits 2, doubles 1, rbi 2, and nothing else is zero unless the owner says the whole line is complete.
6. Pitching lines: on the same stat_line if the player also batted. Innings arrive as "6.2": store outs_pitched 20. Decisions (wins_pitching, losses_pitching, saves, holds, blown_saves) are stored from the box score or the owner's word; never derive them. earned_runs excludes the automatic runner's run. pitches and strikes when given (always ask for pitches in a youth league with a pitch-count table).
7. Suspended or stopped games: follow the pack's Forfeits and abandonments chunk; when a game stops short, ask one question ("is it being resumed, replayed or does it count as a called game?") and log what is known first.
8. Officials, when named: OFFICIATED with the pack's roles. Ejections in a lore chunk titled "Ejections".
9. Story: lore on the event, titled Summary, Key moments, Conditions, Notes, in the owner's words. Anything about anyone's body is left out with one line saying so.
10. Season lines: update each player's and both teams' season lines in the same breath (rule/stats Aggregating): wins/losses/runs_for/runs_against and the split keys (home/away, division/league/interleague from the opponents' COMPETES_IN conference and group, one-run, extra-innings, streak, last-10), games_booked if any match line exists. as_of the game date, source derived.

lore.title: Averages people will quote
lore.content:
Averages people quote after a game, and how to say them honestly:
Batting average, OBP, SLG, OPS: from season lines, over games where the components are non-null; "hitting .341 across the 14 games with a book, 44 at bats". Below the pro level apply the House rules qualifying minimum, default 2 plate appearances per team game.
ERA and WHIP: from outs_pitched, so 41.2 innings is 125 outs and ERA = ER*9/(125/3). Say the innings in thirds notation. In a seven-inning league keep ERA per nine unless House rules say per seven.
Streaks and splits: from COMPETED_IN edges in date order; a suspended game counts on its completion date; a postponed game does not break a streak.
Games back and the wild card: only when every team's games are on file; otherwise give the owner's team's record and say the rest is not on file.
Team pitch counts and rest (youth): read the House rules table, the pitcher's pitches in the last four days from match lines, and the schedule, then answer "eligible" or "not until <date>", nothing more.
Leaders: rule/stats Leaders and records; state the as_of date and the number of lines compared.
Forecasts, projections and anything the record does not hold: say it is not on file.

properties.trigger: options, recalls, call-ups, designated for assignment, waivers, outrights, injured list placements and activations, 26-man and 40-man rosters, trades with cash or players to be named later, affiliates, the amateur draft, the winter unprotected-player draft

data.short_description: Baseball's roster moves as dated events with the edge changes each implies: options and recalls through the loan pattern, lists as designations with no reasons, waivers and DFA, trades with PTBNL and cash, affiliates as teams PART_OF the parent.

lore.title: Moves and their edges
lore.content:
Every move the owner records is an event plus the PLAYS_FOR changes it implies (rule/rosters_and_staff Moves are events). Baseball adds one-team list moves that are neither signings nor releases nor trades: event_type roster_move. Name the event "<Player> — <move> — <YYYY-MM-DD>" and tag it baseball, transaction, the team's slug fragment and the season tag. INVOLVED_IN from the person with role subject and detail naming the move in the vocabulary below, from the team with role to_team or from_team as fits (both for an option: the parent from_team, the affiliate to_team).
Move vocabulary for detail, and the edge change for each:
option: parent edge stays open (role reserve, roster_list forty_man), affiliate PLAYS_FOR opened with arrangement loan, acquired_via option; options_used +1 on the player's season line
recall: affiliate edge ended, parent edge role restored (bench/rotation/starter), roster_list active
outright: parent edge roster_list cleared and role reserve or edge ended per the owner's preference; affiliate edge opened with acquired_via outright
dfa: roster_list dfa, availability unavailable; nothing else changes for up to seven days
waiver_claim: old club's edge ended; new club's PLAYS_FOR opened with acquired_via waiver; event has from_team and to_team
il_placement: roster_list il_10/il_15/il_60, availability unavailable, role injured_reserve; detail "15-day IL, retroactive to <date>" and nothing about why
il_transfer: roster_list changed (il_15 to il_60); detail "transferred to 60-day IL"
activation: roster_list active, availability available, role restored
call_up: a player added to the 40-man and active roster from an affiliate who was not already on the 40-man (contract selected); affiliate edge ended, parent edge opened or updated with roster_list active
september_addition: an active-roster addition under the 28-man expansion; roster_list active
restricted_list, suspended_list: roster_list value and availability unavailable or suspended; a league suspension's stated length and policy name in lore on the person, nothing about the substance of it
paternity_or_bereavement: availability unavailable with no list name and no lore; say nothing more
unprotected_draft_selection, unprotected_draft_return: the winter draft of players left off reserve lists; detail with the clubs; edges per waiver_claim and its reverse
retirement: every open edge ended, person status retired
Trades: one trade event named "<Team A> / <Team B> trade — <date>", INVOLVED_IN each team role other with detail "sends: ... / receives: ...", each player traded_away or acquired with detail the destination; cash considerations and players to be named later as text in the team's detail ("PTBNL"), the named player added later with his own edge and a dated lore line. International bonus pool space and draft picks (competitive-balance picks are the only tradeable ones at the top level) are text in detail. A three-team trade is one event with three team edges.
Signings and releases follow the base: signing (acquired_via free_agent, fee as text: "2y/$30M", "minor-league deal with spring invite", "split contract"), release (edge ended, person status free_agent if no other open playing edge). A minor-league free agent signs with the affiliate team; a major-league deal signs with the parent.

lore.title: Checks, affiliates and what is never recorded
lore.content:
Checks the AI makes when asked, never enforces: active roster count against the level's limit (26, 28 in September, 13 pitchers max until September), 40-man count, options_used against the season cap (five), option years used (three; a lore chunk on the person titled "Option years" lists them), two-way eligibility from season lines, the trade deadline date, waiver and DFA windows (seven days) from the event dates.
Affiliates: each affiliate is a team entity PART_OF the parent franchise with team_type franchise and a tag for its level (aaa, aa, high_a, single_a, complex, rookie), and it competes in its own competition (a minor league, which also needs this pack's APPLIES_TO edge). A player's affiliate edge carries arrangement loan so the base loan pattern finds the parent.
What is never recorded: the reason for any injured-list placement, its expected length, rehab assignments as anything other than a plain option-style affiliate edge (no detail, nothing about why), medical clearances, or anything typed in parentheses after a list name. One line, once, when it comes up: "I've got the list and the date down; this world keeps nothing about why."
Fantasy roster moves are rule/app_fantasy's; a real-world IL placement is what makes a fantasy IL slot legal, so the fantasy edge's slot IL is checked against the real edge's roster_list when the owner asks.
